blocking.issue: The guard keeps a DR5 outcome, and DR2's pi bound, computed from an undefined registered pi_small. This happens when a size passes the guard's two-session test (at least one scored base record in each session) but no task has both harness cells scored in both sessions. Example: DR0 fires on A1-4B-S2 after only a handful of episodes, for instance when the engine dies early. Then X_4B and pi_4B are all-NaN, and the frozen code silently uses pi_small = pi_9B under the 'mean of pi_4B and pi_9B' label against M_SMALL 0.13. That is dry-run bug B3 recurring in an incomplete case.
blocking.evidence: My own scenario w_4bs2_tiny (seed 307, real frozen plan, A1-4B-S2 cut by USR1 after 4 scored base episodes, 0 tasks with both harnesses in S2) was run through every RUNBOOK block, as written, on a fake host. In report-guarded.json primary: X_4B and pi_4B are null; pi_small equals pi_9B; pi_small_rule is 'mean of pi_4B and pi_9B'. There is no pi_small_rule_note and no registered_pi_small_defined. DR5 is {'M': 0.13, 'outcome': 'NO-GO', 'share': 'pi_small'} and DR2 is 'Present', with no note on either. The guard's reading says "4B's session test, DR1, DR5 kept as the registered code computes them". s15.json secondary_corrected has the same DR5. An in-process run reproduces it (scratch verify-d59-1/tiny/v_4bs2_tiny-0.97/A/report/report-guarded.json; runbook run under verify-d59-1/sc/w_4bs2_tiny/host/q2-stage1/analysis/s1a-v1/). D59 (ii) says DR5 is not evaluable as registered when DR0 fires for a session-2 job. D61 (a) keeps every statistic when both sessions hold records, on the stated premise that only a one-session size yields statistics from all-NaN data. Here pi_4B is all-NaN while 4B holds both sessions, so the premise fails. The 9B analogue is already handled: with 4B single, X is all-NaN, so DR2 is not estimable and DR5 is masked.
blocking.minimal_fix: In run_report.mask_block, take the sizes whose per-size pi is undefined from pooled_sizes(y)['pi_mean_4B_9B'], which is already computed. Apply the one-session pi handling to those sizes too: DR5 'not evaluable as registered' with the pi_9B description against both M, registered_pi_small_defined, pi_small_rule_note, DR2's incomplete_note, and the kept_as_registered reading. Keep the session-test masking keyed to one-session sizes. Add a test with a short A1-4B-S2 whose S2 records never pair both harnesses on a task. Record this reading as a one-line addendum to D61 (a) before runbook step 6 runs.

non_blocking: RUNBOOK step 3's poll block (squeue/grep/wc) does not source env.sh. From a fresh ssh, $A is empty and it globs /rescore-*; my emulation printed 'No such file' for both. The runbook says every step also works from a fresh ssh command. Prepend the '. .../env.sh' line.

RUNBOOK step 9's single block runs 'glmm_inputs.py collect' straight after 'submit'. On the host sbatch returns at once and the fits take about 20 min. Pasted whole, collect writes glmm-summary.json with no exit codes and no lock, then exits 3, which is a listed stop condition, and the write-once rule forces a move-aside. Split collect into its own block run after squeue shows none-running, or make it refuse while either .exit file is missing.

D61 (ef8c30d on main) now ratifies the two readings that RUNBOOK step 6 and run_report.INTERPRETATION say 'must be recorded in a program decision'. The branch is based on d3888af and lacks D61. Merge main and cite D61.

Steps 7-10 need step 6's Slurm job to have finished, but the runbook does not say to wait for exit_status=0 first. Running step 7 early writes a failing identity.json (exit 3), which is write-once.

assemble_s15 orders step-count keys numerically, but O.dumps(sort_keys=True) re-sorts them lexicographically ('10' before '3'). Cosmetic only.
report-guarded.json does not itself embed versions or the plan check. provenance.json binds it by digest, which I accept as D59 (iii)'s 'the report carries its provenance'.
